notes.meaning: The writer calls every person on earth to stop and listen carefully. Rich and poor, famous and ordinary people alike need to hear what he has to say. The realities of life and death affect every human being in the exact same way.

The speaker explains that his teaching comes from deep reflection, not careless speech. He has spent time thinking over the truth and wants to pass on genuine wisdom. True understanding begins when we let God shape our thoughts.

Before speaking to others, the psalmist listens closely to the wisdom God reveals to him. He sets this puzzling question of life to the sound of a harp. Music helped people pay attention and remember hard lessons.

The psalmist asks why he should be terrified when evil days come and enemies try to trip him up. Godly people do not need to panic even when proud bullies surround them. God watches over His own people and will bring justice in His own time.

Worldly people place all their confidence in their money and brag about how much they own. They foolishly think their great wealth can protect them from every trouble in life. Riches become an idol whenever someone counts on them instead of trusting God.

No amount of money can buy a person's life back from the grave or pay a ransom to God. Even the richest man cannot purchase an extra day of life for his own brother. Money has zero power to change God's appointed end for human life.

The price to redeem a human life is far higher than any earthly fortune could ever afford. Money simply cannot pay that debt, so all human attempts to buy life must stop forever. Only God has the power to save what money cannot buy.

Wealth cannot guarantee that anyone will live forever without seeing decay in the grave. Even if a wealthy person lived for centuries, physical death would still catch up with him. Eternal life is a gift that cannot be bought with gold or silver.

Anyone can look around and see that wise thinkers and foolish people all end up dying alike. When their lives end, they must leave every bit of their wealth behind for others to use. Earthly belongings cannot follow a person past the grave.

Proud people secretly imagine that their grand estates and family names will last forever on the earth. They even name lands after themselves so that future generations will remember them. In reality, a dark grave becomes the only permanent home their bodies possess.

No matter how much honor and success a person enjoys, he cannot remain in this world. A human life stays here no longer than a traveler stopping at an inn for a single night. In bodily death, wealthy people perish just like the animals.

Trusting in money and dreaming of earthly fame is total foolishness. Even so, each new generation repeats the exact same mistake and praises the sayings of those who went before them. People keep following the misguided habits of their ancestors instead of learning from their end.

The wicked are gathered into the grave like helpless sheep, with death acting as their shepherd. Their earthly beauty and stately mansions decay into dust beneath the ground. But in the morning of God's final triumph, the upright will rise to rule over them.

other.label: Modern scholarship
other.view: Some scholars interpret 'the morning' not as the final resurrection, but as a metaphor for a sudden change of circumstances in this life or an allusion to morning court sessions.

notes.meaning: While human money cannot save anyone, God Himself will rescue the believer from the power of the grave. The writer has complete confidence that God will take him safely to Himself. Death cannot break the eternal bond between God and His people.

Believers should not feel troubled or envious when an ungodly person grows wealthy and adds to his splendor. A sinner's success in this world is only temporary and will soon be over. We have no reason to doubt God's justice when we see wicked people thrive.

When a rich man dies, he leaves this world with completely empty hands. Not one coin of his fortune or shred of his earthly glory goes down into the grave with him. Possessions have zero value once a life is over.

While alive, the selfish man flatters himself and boasts that he is truly happy. Other people praise him too, because the world always honors those who get ahead. But worldly applause cannot change what happens when life comes to a close.

In the end, the ungodly person joins his ancestors in the grave and never sees the light of day again. All the bright comforts and pleasures he enjoyed on earth are snuffed out completely. He is cut off from the light of life forever.

A person who enjoys wealth and honor but lacks spiritual understanding is no better off than the beasts that perish. Living only for physical comfort without knowing God wastes the true purpose of being human. Lasting honor comes from knowing the Lord, not from dying with great possessions.
